explain.say: When the electrons fall back, they give out the extra energy as light of exact wavelengths. Each metal has its own wavelengths, so each glows its own colour.

draw.note: Each metal gives out light of its own wavelengths

faq.q: Which metals make which firework colours?
faq.a: Strontium makes red, sodium yellow-orange, calcium orange, barium green, copper blue, and a mix of strontium and copper makes purple.

faq.q: How do electrons make coloured light?
faq.a: Heat lifts electrons to higher energy levels. When they fall back, they release that energy as light, and the size of the drop decides the colour.
asks: Why do heated metals glow colours?

faq.q: Why are blue fireworks the hardest to make?
faq.a: Copper compounds give blue only within a narrow range of temperatures. Too hot and they break down and the blue washes out, so the mixture must be just right.
asks: Why are there few blue fireworks?

faq.a: In a school lab you hold a bit of a metal compound in a hot flame and watch the colour. Each metal gives its own colour, which identifies it.
asks: How do you do a flame test?

faq.a: Some shells hold a fast-burning powder sealed tight. It turns into hot gas almost instantly, bursting the case and sending out a shock wave we hear as a bang.
asks: What makes the loud bang in fireworks?

facts: Strontium gives fireworks red, barium green, copper blue and sodium yellow.
